title: Instabilities of Fermi Liquids with Arbitrary Forward Scattering: Exact Approach
authors: Dmitry Miserev, Joel Hutchinson, Herbert Schoeller, Jelena Klinovaja, Daniel Loss
abstract: In this work, we consider $N$-fold degenerate $D$-dimensional electron gas with spherical Fermi surface and arbitrary forward-scattering density-density interaction transferring small momentum compared to the Fermi momentum $k_{\mathrm{F}}$. The dimensional reduction that is mathematically equivalent to the Haldane patch construction and similar multidimensional bosonization techniques, provides a natural map of two-point $D$-dimensional correlation functions (fermion Green function, susceptibilities etc.) onto effective one-dimensional (1D) correlators with the same diagrammatic structure, which can be evaluated exactly within a 1D bosonizable (Gaussian) theory. We then apply this formalism to evaluate the fermion Green function, pair and charge/flavor susceptibilities, as well as the composite correlation functions for the case of a finite-range interaction, where the interaction range $R_{\mathrm{s}} \gg 1/k_{\mathrm{F}}$ is large compared to the Fermi wavelength. First, we find that the single-particle spectral function remains Fermi-liquid-like which is fully consistent with the previous research. In contrast to the single-particle sector, the many-body channels are efficiently dressed by finite-range interactions, and this dressing is fully equivalent to the one-loop renormalization group (RG), which is also in line with previous multidimensional bosonization results. Within the forward-scattering model, stable long-range order is not possible, and relevant susceptibilities demonstrate singular power-law scaling with temperature $T$ at $T \to 0$. The rest of the abstract is in the PDF.
summary: This paper develops an exact theoretical framework using dimensional reduction to analyze interacting Fermi liquids with forward scattering. By mapping the problem onto solvable 1D bosonic theories, the authors show that while single-particle physics remains stable, many-body instabilities are enhanced by interactions, predicting specific superconducting or density wave instabilities in certain regimes.
main_problem: The work investigates the instabilities of Fermi liquids when subjected to arbitrary forward-scattering density-density interactions in D dimensions.
main_result: While single-particle properties remain Fermi-liquid-like, many-body channels are significantly dressed by finite-range interactions, leading to singular power-law scaling for relevant susceptibilities at low temperatures. Stable long-range order is generally not possible from forward scattering alone.
method: The authors employ a dimensional reduction technique, mapping D-dimensional correlation functions onto effective 1D correlators which are then evaluated exactly using a 1D bosonizable (Gaussian) theory.
model_or_system: The system is an N-fold degenerate D-dimensional electron gas with a spherical Fermi surface, interacting via small momentum transfer forward-scattering interactions. The analysis extends to finite-range interactions ($R_{\mathrm{s}} \gg 1/k_{\mathrm{F}}$).
key_observables: Fermion Green function, pair susceptibility ($\chi_{2e}$), charge/flavor susceptibilities ($\chi_{2k_F}$, $\chi_{2N k_F}$), and the single-particle spectral function.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T 	o 0$), interaction range ($R_{\mathrm{s}}$), dimensionality ($D$), and degeneracy ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on dimensional reduction techniques equivalent to Haldane patch construction, assuming a spherical Fermi surface, and performing calculations in the leading order of $(kR_s)^{-1}$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies dimensional reduction to map D-dimensional correlation functions onto 1D bosonizable theories. It first confirms single-particle Fermi liquid behavior, then analyzes how many-body susceptibilities are dressed by interactions, concluding with specific predictions for composite instabilities like $4e$ superconductivity.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of dimensional reduction and bosonization techniques to study correlation functions in higher dimensions provides powerful analytical tools applicable to strongly correlated electron models where mean-field or simple RPA approaches fail.
